newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil gains trimmed by late soybean sell-off.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil gains trimmed by late soybean sell-off.

text.p: CBOT soyoil prices ended higher Tuesday on soyoil yield data from the National Oilseed Processors Association, but late losses in soybean futures pared gains, CBOT traders said.
"Oil was up on the crush. The oil content was down to 10.79 (lbs per bushel) from 11.08," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
The soyoil yield data was released Monday in NOPA's monthly crush report for November.
Throughout the harvest, there has been talk that soyoil yields were disappointing, and the NOPA data confirmed that talk, traders said.
Soymeal futures were under pressure mostly from profit taking on the soyoil/soymeal spread following Monday's sharp gains, floor traders said.
Some weakness in both markets was tied to soybean crushers who were buying soybeans and selling soy products, traders said.

CBOT soyoil futures ended up 0.10 to 0.03 cent per lb, with January up 0.04 at 23.36 cents and March up 0.04 cent per lb at 23.80 cents. Soymeal settled down $1.20 to $2.70 a ton with January down $2.40 at $228.90.
